root_cause.text: A race in nvme_poll_irqdisable() recomputed pci_irq_vector() before disable_irq() and again before enable_irq(), so concurrent nvme_dev_disable() changing pdev->msix_enabled could make the function disable one IRQ vector and re-enable a different one, breaking IRQ depth accounting.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states pdev can be disabled between the two calls, causing pci_irq_vector() to return an MSI-X IRQ for disable_irq() and an INTx IRQ for enable_irq(), and the patch fixes this by storing the IRQ in a local variable (`irq = pci_irq_vector(...); disable_irq(irq); ... enable_irq(irq);`).

intent_record.intent_summary: Cache the NVMe queue IRQ vector before polling so the same IRQ is disabled and re-enabled consistently.
intent_record.what: In nvme_poll_irqdisable(), a new local variable `int irq;` is added, the result of `pci_irq_vector(pdev, nvmeq->cq_vector)` is stored once in `irq`, and the existing direct calls `disable_irq(pci_irq_vector(...))` and `enable_irq(pci_irq_vector(...))` are replaced with `disable_irq(irq)` and `enable_irq(irq)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the same IRQ number is now computed once and reused for both disabling and re-enabling the interrupt around CQ polling, ensuring the matching enable operation uses the exact same vector value obtained before polling instead of recalculating it afterward.

grouping_result.intent: Cache the NVMe queue IRQ vector before polling so the same IRQ is disabled and re-enabled consistently.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the race root cause by caching the IRQ vector so nvme_poll_irqdisable() disables and re-enables the same vector even if pdev->msix_enabled changes concurrently.

candidates.rationale: This computes the IRQ vector at disable time from mutable PCI/MSI-X state. If nvme_dev_disable() concurrently changes pdev->msix_enabled, this call may disable a different vector than the one later re-enabled.

This recomputes the IRQ vector again at enable time instead of using the same cached vector used for disable_irq(). Under concurrent state changes, it can re-enable a different IRQ and break IRQ depth accounting.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement recomputes the IRQ vector from mutable PCI/MSI-X state at the time interrupts are disabled. If concurrent nvme_dev_disable() changes pdev->msix_enabled, the vector selected here may differ from the one later used for re-enable, causing mismatched IRQ depth accounting.

This statement recomputes the IRQ vector again instead of reusing the exact vector previously disabled. Under concurrent changes to pdev->msix_enabled, it can re-enable a different IRQ than the one disabled, directly causing the race and depth-accounting inconsistency.
